name: BSc Microbiology
title: BSc Microbiology
intro: The microbiology roadmap: admission, microbiology and immunology papers, lab techniques and careers in pharma, food and healthcare.

phases.title: Class 11–12 subjects
phases.summary: Science with Biology and Chemistry is the standard requirement.
points: Most universities require Class 12 PCB.
Build basics in Biology and Chemistry and learn about hygiene and infectious disease.
Observe how labs work through school visits or science fairs.
Check university labs and hospital or industry tie-ups.

phases.title: Entrance exams and admission
phases.summary: CUET-UG for central universities, merit or entrance for others.
points: Take CUET-UG with the required science subjects.
Apply through the counselling portal of your target university.
State and private colleges often admit by merit.
Prefer colleges with well-equipped labs.

phases.title: Year 1: foundation papers
phases.summary: Core science papers and lab skills.
points: Core papers: Introduction to Microbiology, Biochemistry, Cell Biology and Chemistry.
Under NEP you also take language, environment and skill-enhancement courses.
Learn to maintain a lab notebook, follow safety rules and write practical reports.
Start reading beyond the syllabus and attend department seminars.

phases.title: Year 2–3: advanced and applied papers
phases.summary: Deeper papers, electives and a project.
points: Year 2: Bacteriology, Virology, Mycology, Immunology and Microbial Genetics.
Year 3: Medical Microbiology, Industrial and Food Microbiology, Environmental Microbiology, Biotechnology and a project.
Complete a project or dissertation under a faculty guide.
Many universities offer a fourth Honours year with research.

phases.title: Lab skills, internships and training
points: Learn: sterile technique, culturing and staining, antibiotic sensitivity testing, microbial analysis of food and water and quality control methods.
Do summer internships or short research projects in labs, companies and government institutions.
Take certificate courses on SWAYAM, NPTEL or industry bodies.
Keep a record of your projects, certificates and skills.

phases.title: After BSc: MSc, exams and careers
phases.summary: Master’s degree, NET/JRF, government jobs or industry.
points: Further study and careers: MSc Microbiology, pharma and food quality control, clinical microbiology labs, research and vaccine development.
Exams: CUET-PG, CSIR-UGC NET, GAT-B/BET and state recruitment for lab posts.
Research route: MSc, then CSIR-UGC NET (JRF) or GATE and a PhD.
Government exams such as SSC and state PSCs are open to science graduates.
facts: CUET-PG, CSIR-UGC NET, GAT-B/BET and state recruitment for lab posts
